defects.issue: The drill reloads its images whenever the parent re-renders. The parent builds `sources` (and so DualPlayer's `left`/`right` props) as new objects on every render. DualPlayer's effect depends on [left, right, n], so each re-render resets `loaded` to 0, builds new Image objects, restarts the playback clock and calls onReady again. onReady resets `shownAt`. As a result: (a) the first setReady(true) re-render triggers one reload and moves the reaction-time origin; (b) typing in the Reader field during a trial restarts playback and resets `shownAt`, which corrupts the logged rtMs; (c) answering causes a reload, and the loading percentage overlay flashes during the reveal. Mean reaction time is one of the drill's reported statistics.
defects.fix: Memoise the two sources per trial, e.g. useMemo keyed on trial, or pass stable base/frames strings and make the effect depend on `${base}|${n}`. In the parent, set shownAt and ready only on the first onReady of a trial (`if (!ready)`). Better still, keep DualPlayer's load effect independent of parent renders by depending on primitive props.

defects.issue: Capture mode is not enabled. XrayRenderer now has setCaptureMode(on): synchronous histogram read-back, run frames counted per render and recursion cleared at run start. I fixed every high and medium review item, the three low items and the rule violation, and added the missing resolution scope. One item is not fully met: pre-contrast local contrast in the RAO views is still below the original renderer (RAO caudal 11.7 against 20.8). It is recorded as a calibration item with the experiments behind it.

**1. Per-pass timing (high).** The harness's hard sync now reads one pixel from the framebuffer that was just drawn, then restores the bindings. Before, it read the default framebuffer, which on this WebKit/Metal build does not wait for offscreen work. The sync floor is now the cost of a do-nothing timed section (clear and read a 1x1 target), measured every frame and subtracted. In timer-query mode the harness times every 8th frame between syncs by itself, so it flags implausible timer results without help from the caller (on this machine: 70 ms of timer sums against a 12.7 ms frame).

**2. Cost (medium).** I withdrew the old 0.9 ms claim and re-measured at 768 and 1024.
- Serialised, the S2 chain costs 2.1-2.7 ms at 768 and 2.2-3.0 ms at 1024.
- A new 1x1 pass computes the auto-exposure meter value once per frame, which cut the detector pass from 0.8-0.9 ms to 0.3-0.4 ms.
- Serialised numbers overstate, so the frame total comes from a pipelined loop: 4.2-4.7 ms per frame at 768 and 7.2-8.2 ms at 1024, which is borderline on the plan's 8 ms. The original renderer measured 3.6-7.3 ms and 5.8-7.9 ms in the same minutes, with machine load varying 2-3x.
- The anatomy pass (another stream's clutter code) is now the largest single cost.

**3. Profile A noise ratio (medium).** I added an optional dark-side weighting of the noise floor and refitted profile A's split between quantum noise and floor on six views. The dark/bright noise ratio is now 1.13-1.24 in every view (target 1.1-1.3; before 1.03-1.17).

**4. Local contrast (medium).** I tried six processing variants. None restores RAO caudal without breaking the per-view median grey or overshooting LAO cranial. The cause is the anatomy's grey distribution in that view, so I kept the processing and recorded the numbers and the variant table for the integration stream. A median-band window option is ready for that re-tune.

I fixed every item in the review: both medium defects and all three low ones. Nothing outside `src/render/xray/segments/` and my two docs files was edited, and there was nothing to revert. The pass is still off by default behind the feature flag. Typecheck is clean for my files and all 34 tests pass in about 13 s.

**What was wrong with the real-tree errors.** I re-ran the old code on the then-current tree:

| Version | Rays | p95 | p99 | Worst |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Old code | 438 | 1.08 % | 3.13 % | 20.8 % |
| Host ranges only, before the family pass | 450 | 1.04 % | 10.9 % | 43 % |

The reviewer's "worst 28.986 %" mixed three causes:
- **Crossing branches.** Siblings and cousins running into each other away from their origins (mostly the PDA twigs) caused every ray over 5 %.
- **Too few host slots.** Origin double counting from the 3-slot limit gave errors of a few per cent.
- **The reference itself.** The old test marched at 0.05 mm, up to a third of a small twig's radius. Re-marching the disagreeing rays 8 times finer matched the integrator, for example D1: coarse 0.1657, fine 0.16309, integrator 0.1631.

**What changed**
- **Branch origins (medium).** A host slot can now hold one segment, a run of up to 31 consecutive segments, or a pointer to an extension list in a small side texture. A branch's first 16 segments subtract the whole run of parent segments they overlap. The longest run on three trees was 8.
- **Vessel families (new).** Any other overlap inside one coronary tree is now counted once: crossing siblings, cousins, a branch re-entering its parent, a twig reaching its grandparent. Each segment has a priority (tree depth, then tube, then index) and subtracts only higher-priority overlapping segments, so the relations cannot loop. Nothing was left unresolved on five trees or on the PCI scene.
- **Frame-to-frame reuse.** A new option, `topologyFrom`, reuses the previous frame's branch links. Conversion drops from 3.0-4.1 ms to 0.85-0.9 ms in Node, and from 6.1 to 1.3 ms in the browser for the full scene.
- **Honest test bounds (medium).** The tests now bound p99 and the worst ray, classify every ray over 1 %, and cast three rays through the first segments of every branch.
- **Back-fill (low).** It only runs at joints `addChain` made, only when the neighbour exists and shares the joint point. A test feeds planes at the first and last index: no NaN.
- **Velocity (low).** Unlisted segments keep their centre-ray velocity, and listed ones are averaged over the same sub-samples as their attenuation.
- **Binning (low).** Tile counts use 2D difference arrays, and an adaptive block pre-cull skips off-screen runs of 32 segments. The test now bounds time as a ratio to a minimal reference loop (5.3-5.6 measured, bound 10).

**Handed to S3b.** I left a note for S3b (the tree generator) in my notes file. Each tree has 5-7 twigs that re-enter their parent and 29-37 pairs of separate branches that interpenetrate. The integrator now unites them, but the anatomy is wrong.

**Speed.** On the shared M-series GPU at 768 px, vessels (2,655 segments) take 1.8-2.5 ms with anti-aliasing and 0.8 ms without. Everything (5,543 segments) takes 3.5-3.7 ms. The 15 frames/s target holds.

The notes file has the exact sceneBuilder change. It now passes the previous frame's batch as `topologyFrom`, keyed by the tree object, which is replaced on every lumen change.

JR4 with clockwise torque engaged in 2/5, and in one start the JR4 never reached the root.

Under the configuration bench.chooseConfig picked on this machine today (segmentScale 1.14 at 120 Hz), JR4 clockwise RCA engagement fell to 1/5, and to 2/5 at the reported scale of 1.37. manoeuvres.test.ts requires at least 3, so the adaptive performance path fails the stream's own acceptance test.

Snapshot/restore is not exact once the hub has been released. After a grip-null spin-back, snapshot, step 1 s, restore, step 1 s, the node buffers differed by up to 3.66 mm. The held, hands and explicitGrip state is not in EngineSnapshot (critique item 21). The same check with the wire loaded gave identical buffers (diff 0).
Worker budget: at the defaults the bench measured 2.01 to 2.28 ms per 15 fps frame for 89 to 103 bodies (my run), against the acceptance of at most 2 ms for about 300 nodes.

defects.issue: The engagement, torque and size manoeuvres pass only at one exact geometry (the rounded fixture) and one numeric configuration. Sub-millimetre geometry changes, or the segment coarsening that chooseConfig applies, flip JL4 and JR4 outcomes below the asserted majorities. The claim that the behaviour emerges from the mechanics is therefore not shown for the geometry and settings the app will actually run with.
defects.fix: Lower the sensitivity: make the trust-region step consistent (see the xpbd defect), and consider more iterations or a smaller trust region. Then run the manoeuvre tests on the live buildAnatomy/aorticCourse geometry and at each segmentScale/substepHz that chooseConfig can return (for example 1.0, 1.2 and 1.4). Alternatively, restrict chooseConfig to settings already shown to preserve the outcomes, and report the success rates per configuration.

defects.issue: The per-body trust region (lines 399-410) scales the applied displacement, but rod.lambda still accumulates the full Δλ (line 413). The multipliers then no longer match the motion. Every iteration where the clamp is active inflates the joint forces read by jointForceOnBody. Those forces drive the hub axial and torsion reactions, the grip-slip limits (4 N and 8 N·mm), the hub spin-back, the contact normal loads N and the friction η, which ties the friction state to the clamp. This is the likely root of the settings-dependence the report admits.
defects.fix: Apply a single step scale s = min(1, maxMove/max|Δx|, maxRot/max|Δθ|) to both the displacement and Δλ. Or, when a body is clamped, recompute Δλ for the displacement actually taken. Add a test that hub axial force under a slow push matches the summed friction plus stiffness reaction when the clamp is active.

defects.issue: snapshot()/restore() omit the hand state (Device.held, hands, explicitGrip). After a grip release, restore resumes with the hub held, so replay diverges (3.66 mm measured). restore() also reloads devices through catheterSpec(id), which throws for catheters built from a custom DeviceSpec such as STRAIGHT6F. The coronary lumen positions set by moveCoronaries are not captured either.
defects.fix: Add held, hands and explicitGrip, plus the coronary tube points or the last MotionInput, to EngineSnapshot. Store the spec, or a factory key, so non-catalogue specs can be restored. Extend the determinism test to cover a released hub and a wire with an inner device.

defects.issue: The defaults exceed the 2 ms budget. chooseConfig is never called by PhysicsHost, the worker or PhysicsClient, and the S7.md store integration snippet passes no config, so the budget is not enforced in practice. The plan's figure of about 300 nodes is not met (about 90 to 120 bodies) and is waved through as 'resolution where it matters'. The engine allocates in hot paths every substep: exitPose and wirePointAt create Float64Arrays, contact.rowsFor builds nested arrays per contact per iteration, and solveDevice creates an opt object. That adds GC jitter in the worker.
defects.fix: Have the worker run a short bench at init, or accept a config from it, and document this in the integration steps. Hoist the per-substep allocations into reusable scratch buffers. Either meet the node-count target or record that the deviation was agreed.

defects.issue: The plan's hub-reaction task asks for per-node contact force and stick-slip events in each step's output, for S14 hazards and S9 pressure. PhysicsFrame/DeviceReadout carry only hub axial, torsion and snap. The engine always sets HubReaction.wedged to false; only the client patches it from dampingRisk. Stick-slip events (the transition from static to kinetic friction in contact.after) are not emitted.
defects.fix: Add a per-node normal-force Float32Array (rod.cN) and a stick-slip event count or flag to DeviceReadout. Set wedged in the engine from the classifier.

defects.fix: Recompute cum (and any cached segment lengths) in moveCoronaries.

I fixed all seven review items: two medium and five low, the low ones including the 12 px design-rule breach. Each fix has a test. 86 tests pass (78 in src/input/input.test.ts and 8 in src/input/views.test.ts), and my files typecheck clean. The review found no edits outside my files and I made none, so nothing needed restoring. The layer is still not wired into the labs, as the brief says, and nothing has been tried on real hardware.

**Medium items**
- **Rumble kept buzzing at the last load (haptics.ts).** The haptics controller now tracks how old the last physics reaction is. Once it is older than 0.3 s it sends one zero effect and then stays silent. In the test, one reaction followed by 10 s of frames gave at most 5 effects at the old load, then one zero effect, then nothing. The review's probe of the same case played 120.
- **releaseAll() missed gamepad, torquer, MIDI and USB switch holders (system.ts).** It now opens the right hand and stops the plunger, and unpins whoever holds the pin. Gamepad and torquer controls that are still held when it runs stay inactive until they are let go and pressed again. MIDI and USB switches already only act on a change. In the test, a gamepad holding a grip, a pin and the cine trigger is fully released, stays released while still held, and works again after a re-press.

**Low items**
- **Torquer brake stayed on.** The brake now uses the same 0.3 s rule, so it drops to 0 when reactions stop. Its report is sent only when it changes (at most every 80 ms, release at once) rather than every frame. In the test, one load then silence sends exactly two reports: brake full, then brake off.
- **Pins.** A pin now counts every source holding it. It lets go only when the last one releases, and a source that does not hold it cannot release it. Old snapshots still restore.
- **Port labels below 12 px (TableView.tsx).** The labels now sit above their stopcocks and are sized from the strip's actual on-screen scale. They render at 12.5 px at strip heights 200, 220, 240 and 300. The middle label moves up a line when the text is large, so neighbours don't touch. I checked the layout by rendering it to SVG and viewing it in Quick Look.
- **USB pedal learning.** Learning now compares two real reports, so a constant status bit in the first report can no longer be taken for the pedal. It also infers whether the device reports continuously or only on change, to get the pedal's on/off direction right.
- **Notes.** The table view's hand updates are now limited to one re-render per animation frame, so the performance statement in the notes is true. Integration step 1 now has a full table of the old lab keys and what clashes. Space, Q/E, Z, P, the up/down arrows and 1-5 clash; X, H, R and V are free.

**Cost:** input frame 0.002-0.004 ms of CPU, table render 0.55-0.8 ms (both under Node). No GPU work, so the 15 frames/s renderer budget is unaffected. The notes file and the facts file are both updated, including the new model parameters.

defects.issue: Rumble never goes stale. HapticsController.step() builds the effect from `this.last` however old it is, and RumbleMapper re-sends a sustained effect every 80 ms. PseudoHapticGain has a staleS cutoff but the rumble path does not. I confirmed this with a probe: one reaction with axial 1.2 followed by 10 s of step() calls and no new reactions played 120 effects, each at strongMagnitude 0.8. So if the physics pauses, finishes or stops feeding reactions while frame() keeps running (for example on the calibration screen), the controller buzzes at the last load indefinitely.
defects.fix: Track the reaction age in HapticsController the same way PseudoHapticGain does (age += dt, reset on feed). Pass null to rumble.step once age > DEFAULT_PSEUDO.staleS so that one zero effect is sent and the rumble goes silent. Add a test: feed once, step for longer than staleS, and expect the last effect to be zero with nothing played after it.

defects.issue: The torquer brake is held at the last level. `lastAxial` is set only in the reaction listener, never decays, and frame() sends torquerOutputReport(lastAxial) to the device every frame. When reactions stop, the DIY torquer's axial brake stays engaged at its last value. The report is also re-sent every frame even when nothing changed.
defects.fix: Use the same staleness rule as the rumble fix and drive the brake to 0 when the reaction is stale. Send the output report only when its bytes change, or at a capped rate such as the 80 ms rumble interval.

defects.issue: releaseAll() does not release every source, although its doc says "Release every hand and foot (pause, unmount, case end)". It sends releaseSource only for keyboard, mouse, trackpad and ui. A grip held by a gamepad stick (holder 'gamepad:N'), a torquer grip button, and pins held by gamepad LB/RB, MIDI pinAuto or a HID switch all survive. My probe confirmed it: after a gamepad stick grip, releaseAll() left view().right.gripped === true. On pause or case end, the physics still sees the right hand gripping and the left hand pinning.
defects.fix: In releaseAll, also release the hands directly: clear all holders (HandState.release) and unpin whatever source holds the pin, for example with a HandState.releaseAll() that returns the grip-null and pin-off commands. Reset gamepad and torquer memory so a still-held control has to be re-pressed. Add a test with a gamepad grip and a gamepad pin.

defects.issue: A pin can be released by a source that does not hold it. pinOff unpins when `t === this.pin` even if pinSource is a different source. Case: Q (pin wire) is pressed on the keyboard, then the mouse right button (auto, which resolves to the same wire) takes over pinSource. Releasing Q unpins the wire while the mouse button is still held (confirmed by probe). This weakens the guarantee that a pinned device does not move.
defects.fix: Count the sources holding the pin (a Set of SourceIds, like the right-hand holders) and unpin only when the last holder lets go. Keep the 'stale key-up does not release' test, and add one for two sources pinning the same device.

defects.issue: The port labels 'Pressure', 'Contrast' and 'Saline' are fontSize 12 in a 1200x300 viewBox. At the documented strip heights (200-240 px, so scale at most 0.8) they render at about 8-10 px, which breaks the design-system rule of 12 px minimum.
defects.fix: Size the labels so they render at 12 px or more at the intended strip height (about 16 user units at height 220 or above). Alternatively, scale the text inversely to the rendered size, or move the labels out of the scaled SVG.

defects.issue: HID learn can bind the wrong bit. When the device has sent no earlier report for that report id, `before` is all zeros, so every constant non-zero byte in the first report counts as a change. diffBits returns the lowest byte first, so learning can bind a constant status bit instead of the pedal bit.
defects.fix: Record a baseline report first: ignore the first report seen after learn() starts, or compare only against a recorded previous report. Require a bit that actually toggled between two real reports.

defects.issue: Two statements in the notes are inaccurate. (1) It says TableView "re-renders at most once per animation frame (rAF-coalesced)", but the 'hands' listener calls setHands synchronously on every event. Only the preview path uses the rAF bump. (2) It says the remaining legacy keys collide with nothing "except Z and P". Space was the legacy inject key and is now pinAuto, and the integrator also needs to know that R, X, V and H are free.
defects.fix: Correct the performance statement, or rAF-coalesce the setHands call too. List Space among the conflicts in integration step 1.

ruleViolations: TableView SVG port labels render below the 12 px minimum at the documented strip heights (design-system rule).

I fixed all six review items: both high, both medium and both low. All 393 tests in src/simulation pass, 54 of them in patient.test.ts (8 new), and typecheck shows no errors in S9 files. The review found no ownership violations. This round I edited only S9-owned files; the probe and timing scripts were temporary and have been deleted. The HaemoMonitor colour change has still not been seen in a browser (not allowed for this stream).

- **Dower ECG coefficients (high).** Table 3 of Vondrak and Penhaker 2022 has two misprints: V5 X is printed 2.125 and V4 Z −0.604. I reopened the paper. The same paper's Table 4 (the inverse matrix) is matched exactly only with V5 X = 1.125 and V4 Z = −0.601. The largest error is 0.0005 with the corrected values, against 0.097 with the printed ones. Table 4 is now in ecg12.ts and a test checks the match. A normal beat's R waves are now V4 0.98, V5 1.09 and V6 0.90 mV; before, V5 was 1.79 mV.
- **Stable angina patients ischaemic at rest (high).** Only a thrombotic lesion at 99% or more now stops flow. Chronic occlusions and severe chronic stenoses are fed by collaterals, and chronic disease always leaves at least 1.3 times resting demand. Two other changes keep stable patients quiet:
  - Whether ischaemia is transmural (ST elevation) now depends on how much supply fails at resting demand. Ischaemia from raised demand alone stays subendocardial and shows as ST depression.
  - Adenosine now steals flow from collateral-fed territory (steal fraction 0.5, a model parameter).
  - The engine now takes its resting blood pressure from the 6 s warm-up. This removed a baroreflex, heart rate and pain feedback loop that started at rest in uncalibrated engines.
  - On the reviewer's probe (40 seeds, 120 s), the counts for ischaemia > 0.2, ST of 1 mm or more, STEMI criteria and chest pain went from 14/13/11/16 to 0/0/0/0, with and without calibration.
- **Every ACS total occlusion thrombotic (medium).** Only the culprit occlusion is thrombotic now; the other occlusions are CTOs. On arrival, ischaemia is preloaded only downstream of the culprit lesion. Across 40 STEMI seeds, ischaemia above 0.1 outside the culprit territory went from 9 patients to 0 (largest 0.05). Seed 6 went from 0.44/0.56/0.93 (LAD/LCx/RCA) to 0.00/0.56/0.00. It is left-dominant, so its inferior ST elevation is correct. Seed 4 went from RCA 0.83 to 0.00.
- **Snapshot missing the coronary network (medium).** Snapshots now record the lesions, a fingerprint of the tree and the region count. `restore()` rebuilds the network from trees the engine has seen, or from `restore(snap, { tree })`. It throws a clear error if the tree is missing or the region counts do not match. A test restores across a stenting step and gets byte-identical results.
- **Mid LAD giving inferior elevation (low).** I re-aimed the distal LAD region in the default network and added a D2 region. Mid LAD culprits that also met the inferior criteria went from 17 of 19 to 0 of 19.
- **Hard-coded monitor colours (low).** The alarm banner now uses the notice-danger, notice-warn and notice-info classes. The trace colours are read once from the colour tokens at mount, with plain rgb values kept only as a fallback for server rendering.

defects.issue: Two DOWER coefficients are wrong: V5 X = 2.125 and V4 Z = -0.604. They were copied faithfully from Vondrak and Penhaker 2022 Table 3, but that table contains typos. I checked this against the same paper's Table 4 (the inverse Dower matrix). Its pseudo-inverse of the 8x3 Dower matrix comes out exactly only with V5 X = 1.125 and V4 Z = -0.601. With 2.125 the X row becomes 0.095 ... 0.270 ... 0.113, against the printed 0.156 ... 0.239 ... 0.194. The effect: V5 shows about twice the voltage of V4 and V6 (R wave 1.79 mV against 0.87 and 0.80), and every V5 ST deviation is inflated about 1.9 times. That includes the reported LCx occlusion 'V5 +3.7 mm', and V5 is the monitor's default second lead.
defects.fix: Set V5 to [1.125, 0.127, -0.086] and V4 to [1.213, 0.127, -0.601]. Add a test that the pseudo-inverse of the 8 independent leads reproduces Table 4 to 3 decimals. Note the typo and the cross-check in facts/S9.md. Re-measure the LAD, RCA and LCx ST figures in S9.md.

defects.issue: Stable angina patients become ischaemic at rest, and many reach STEMI criteria. stenosisFactor() (line 296) treats any lesion with severity >= 99 that is not a CTO as an acute occlusion with zero flow (rest 0, hyp 0). The AngioCAD 91-99 band, drawn uniformly, reaches 99, so an SA 'severe-stenosis' at 99% acts as a fresh occlusion with no collaterals (SA seed 7: LAD ischaemia 1.0, ST 6.2 mm, pain 10/10). Lesions of 91-98% are also given no collateral supply, so supplyFor() returns a resting deficit, and that deficit builds transmural ischaemia and chest pain within two minutes. The design intends SA patients to be quiet at rest: preloadAcs() skips SA. The model breaks that, and no test covers it.
defects.fix: Treat only thrombotic or culprit lesions at >= 99% as acute occlusions. Give chronic subtotal and severe stenoses a collateral or minimum resting supply, as CTOs already get, so resting demand is met in SA. Then demand ischaemia appears only when demand rises or hyperaemia is induced, and only as subendocardial ST depression. Add a test: N SA seeds at rest for 120 s show no |ST| >= 1 mm, no STEMI criteria and chest pain near 0.

defects.issue: lesionKind() (line 348) makes every 100% segment 'thrombotic' in UA, NSTEMI and STEMI patients, not just the culprit. 23 of the ACS rows have more than one 100% segment, and 131 have at least one. Non-culprit total occlusions, which are usually CTOs with collaterals, are therefore modelled as acute occlusions with zero flow. On top of that, engine.preloadAcs() preloads ischaemia in every region with deficit > 0.3, not only the culprit territory. In the probe, STEMI seed 6 arrives with three-territory ischaemia and seed 4 (Mid LAD culprit) with RCA ischaemia 0.83 and MAP 68. The STEMI arrival test only checks that some lead is above 1 mm, not the territory.
defects.fix: Mark only the culprit 100% segment as thrombotic and make the others 'cto' (collateral-supplied). Restrict preloadAcs() to regions downstream of the culprit lesion. Extend the STEMI test to assert that the elevated lead group matches the culprit territory and that non-culprit territories are not ischaemic.

report.summary:
I fixed all five review findings and both rule violations. Typecheck reports no errors in any S11 file, and all 55 mentor tests pass (48 before, 7 new). As before, S11 is not wired into the labs this wave. The review found no ownership violations, and this revision edited only S11 files.

**Injection quality through the store bridge (the medium finding)**
- **The bug:** the bridge hard-coded the injection start at 0 s. In the current diagnostic lab, every cine run therefore failed the pre-contrast check, so any self-rating of 3 or more for injection technique was flagged as over-confident.
- **The fix:**
  - The bridge now sends `injectStartS: null` and marks pre-contrast filming as not measurable, because that store starts the cine and the injection together.
  - `analyse` then sets `preContrastOk` to `null` for those runs; `CineRun.preContrastOk` and `InjectionQuality.preContrastOk` are now `boolean | null`. No code outside S11 reads them.
  - The debrief's injection-technique measure skips the check when it is `null`.
- **Peak time:** this is now measured from the store's live bolus opacity: the first moment it reaches its maximum. The old unlabelled `0.3` survives only as a named fallback, `LEGACY_BOLUS_MODEL.peakPhase`, used when the opacity is not available. It comes from the store's own `advanceBolus` envelope, and that is recorded in facts/S11.md.
- **New bridge test:** it seats the catheter selectively in the real store and makes two clean runs. Each run reports no injection start and a peak at phase 0.3 of the bolus, within one store tick. Pre-contrast comes out as not measurable, wash-out and fill pass, and a self-rating of 5 is measured as 5 and not flagged.
- **Other hosts:** a host that does report an injection start is still graded: 0.1 s fails, 0.6 s passes.

**Target segment and its foreshortening (the other medium finding)**
- **Helpers:** I added two, so the labs need no geometry code of their own:
  - `segmentForeshortening(geometry, label, cArm)` in `coverage.ts` (2.8 µs per call on the real tree).
  - `segmentLabelAt(tree, vessel, position)` in `treeSegments.ts`. It gives a valid LAD, RCA or circumflex segment label for each of the 4 PCI scenario lesions.
- **Notes:** the integration notes now have step 1e for the diagnostic store and an addition to step 2 for the PCI lab. Both are owned by S10 and include exact code, the target choice (the most severe lesion, otherwise the proximal segment of the focus side), and when to recompute: on every cine start and C-arm change. Without this, the foreshortened-view rule stays silent.

**Low findings**
- **Rule thresholds:** every number in `rules.ts` is now a named entry in `MENTOR_PARAMS`.
  - The oversize ratio is read from `ANALYSIS_PARAMS`, so the live attending and the debrief metric always agree. A test checks the stop just above and just below that ratio.
  - The 0.7 foreshortening trigger is kept deliberately below the coverage threshold of 0.8: the attending interrupts only for a clearly foreshortened view and leaves borderline views to the debrief. It is now listed in facts/S11.md with that reason.
  - The bridge's 0.5 s C-arm rest time is also named, as `BRIDGE_PARAMS.viewRestS`.
- **Saved recordings:** a new `recording-index` store (IndexedDB schema version 2) holds one small summary per attempt. Saving, trimming and listing now read only that index, and a full recording loads only when opened. Recordings saved under the old schema are indexed the first time the list is read. Reading a whole store now takes one transaction instead of one request per record.
- **Benchmark import:** a file is now rejected if the chosen rule needs a value that is missing, for example `sd` under `mean+sd`, or `min` and `max` under `max`. It also checks that `n` is a whole number and the other statistics are numbers.
  - The "n =" label counts only the metrics that are kept.
  - A benchmark-based standard set now always keeps the zero-critical-errors standard, marked critical.

`npx tsc --noEmit -p .` exits cleanly but checks nothing, because the root tsconfig lists no files, so I typechecked with `tsconfig.app.json` instead. I added no GPU cost; the only new per-frame CPU work is the 2.8 µs foreshortening call, and it runs only on a cine start or a view change.

defects.issue: diffEvents hard-codes `injectStartS: 0` on every cine-end. analysis.ts then sets preContrastOk = (0 >= minPreContrastS 0.27) = false for every run recorded through the store bridge, which is the only path the current diagnostic lab will use. The debrief's 'Injection technique' measure in DIAGNOSTIC_SUBSKILLS therefore always comes out 0, mapped to 1.0 on the 1-5 scale. Any learner who rates themselves 3 or higher is flagged 'You rated this higher than the record shows', for a pre-contrast filming step the legacy lab gives them no way to do (its bolus starts with the injection). The same line also sets `peakS: p.bolus.duration * 0.3`, an unlabelled constant that is not named as a model parameter, which breaks the no-invented-numbers rule. The bridge test does not catch either problem.
defects.fix: Leave injectStartS out, or mark pre-contrast as not measurable (preContrastS null, so it is excluded from the measure) when the host cannot film before the injection. Have the 'inject' sub-skill measure skip runs whose preContrastS is null. Either get peakS from the store's bolus model or name the 0.3 fraction as a model parameter in ANALYSIS_PARAMS and in facts/S11.md. Add a bridge test asserting that injection-quality calibration is not penalised.

defects.issue: The integration notes never say how the lab should fill MentorInput.targetForeshortening and targetSegment, which context.ts reads and the 'foreshortened-view' starter rule depends on. As written, wiring per the notes leaves one of the ten starter rules permanently silent. The notes list every MentorInput.pci field but not these two.
defects.fix: Add an integration step: on a cine start or a view change, compute targetForeshortening = foreshortening(polys of the target label from treeSegmentGeometry(tree), cameraBasis(cArm)) and pass targetSegment, with the target label taken from the case focus or the PCI lesion segment. Name the owner (S10 labs).

defects.issue: Rule thresholds are inlined and duplicated instead of coming from the named parameter sets. The foreshortened-view trigger uses `< 0.7`, while coverage uses minForeshortening 0.8, and 0.7 is missing from the facts file's model-parameter list. The oversized-balloon rule repeats `> 1.1` instead of reading ANALYSIS_PARAMS.oversizeRatio, so a calibration change would make the live attending and the debrief metric disagree.
defects.fix: Read the thresholds from ANALYSIS_PARAMS and DEFAULT_COVERAGE, or a named MENTOR_PARAMS object, and list the 0.7 trigger in facts/S11.md under model parameters.

defects.issue: saveRecording calls trimStore, which calls getAll, which does a sequential get of every stored record. With 50 records (about 600 kB each, roughly 30 MB) that whole deserialisation runs on every save. listRecordings also loads every full record and rebuilds a FrameTable for each one just to read the duration. The end-of-case and history-list pauses grow with storage.
defects.fix: Keep a small metadata index (id, startedAt, durationS, bytes) in a separate key or store. Trim and list from the index, and load full records only on demand.

defects.issue: importBenchmark validates mean and n but not sd, min or max. A file without sd under rule 'mean+sd', or without min and max under rule 'max', yields NaN thresholds, and those standards then fail silently. The source label uses Math.min(n) across all metrics, including n = 0 entries that are later filtered out, so it can read 'n = 0'. A benchmark-derived set also drops the critical-error standard.
defects.fix: Validate that sd, min and max are finite numbers when the rule needs them. Compute the label n over the kept metrics only. Keep the critical-errors standard, marked critical, alongside the benchmark-derived standards.

src/mentor/rules.ts: the foreshortened-view trigger 0.7 is a model parameter that facts/S11.md does not list.

report.summary:
I fixed both medium review items and all four low ones. No ownership or rule violations were reported, and every edit stayed inside S13's owned files. `npx vitest run src/content` passes: 53 passed, plus the per-author track check, which is skipped by design. The whole project type-checks with zero errors. Browser checks were still not allowed, so the drill cards and set reports were checked by server-side rendering in the tests.

**Medium fixes**
- **Find the lesion grades the wrong lesion.** A hit is now graded against the box the learner clicked, not the worst lesion on the frame. Where boxes overlap, the box whose centre is nearest the click counts. The prompt now reads "Click a stenosis… grade the lesion you clicked", and the explanation lists every box on the frame with its grade. After answering, the highlighted grade and the verdict follow the box that was hit. Two tests cover this: a made-up frame with two boxes in different grade bins, and all 70 library frames with mixed bins (103 of 269 keyframes have more than one box).
- **Occluded RCA? and Collaterals? could be answered from the image set.** Both drills now use CoronaryDominance main-set runs only. Negatives must carry an explicit "no" tag, come from studies with no run tagged for that finding, and leave out runs flagged uncertain. Each set is 6 positive/negative pairs, each pair from the same image set with the same artefact tag. The artefact tag was a second giveaway: 70 of 72 clean RCA runs carry it, against 11 of 216 occluded runs. Over 20 sets per drill, neither image set nor artefact tag predicts the answer.
  - The cost is a small pool. Occlusion has 13 matched pairs, so runs repeat between sets, and the drill description says so. Collaterals has 41.

**Low fixes**
- **Tests now check the sets themselves.** Every set has equal counts per answer class. A constant answer's raw accuracy equals chance in every stratified drill and in the strict projection set.
  - **Name the projection:** with "accept either name near a boundary", the best constant answer beats chance (all 20 test sets). The set report now shows that figure and points to the strict option.
  - **Plan the next view:** its sets are labelled "Not stratified" in the description and the report, with the best constant answer's score shown.
- **Progress tab:** the dashed line on each learning curve now sits at that drill's chance level, and the table has a new Chance column.
- **Due-for-review mismatch:** real-angiogram reads now use the same spaced-repetition rule as quizzes but are stored under their own key. The dashboard's due count and the Review page therefore agree. Records the earlier build wrote into the quiz memory are moved across once when the drills open. This changes saved progress data at runtime, not the store file.
- **Drill parameters:** they are now applied, not dropped. Allowed: `artery` (LCA or RCA) for the projection, grade, locate and estimate drills, and `borderline` for the projection drill. The validator rejects any other key, value or drill, so a parameter in a lesson always takes effect. The drill shows "From the lesson: …" with an "All runs" button that clears it. I added one diagnostic lesson block that uses this: a strict, left-coronary-only projection set.

The notes file and `datasets/ATTRIBUTION.md` are updated. Integration step 4 (showing due reads on the Dashboard and Review pages) is now optional, and step 6 describes the one-time move of saved records. No new literature constants, so the facts file is unchanged.

defects.issue: Locate drill grades the wrong lesion. scoreLocate counts a click inside any expert box on the frame as a hit (hitBox), but then sets gradeRef to it.answer, which is the worst grade on the whole frame (worstOnFrame). I checked the library: 103 of 269 lesion keyframes have more than one box, and on 70 of them the boxes fall in different grade bins. On those frames, a learner who correctly marks and grades a less severe lesion is told 'Lesion found; expert grade X' and counted wrong. This skews the grading balanced accuracy, weighted kappa and bias in the set report. The prompt also asks for 'the most important stenosis', yet a hit on any box is accepted.
defects.fix: Have scoreLocate use the box that hitBox returns: gradeRef = gradeBin(hitBox(...)[4]). Alternatively, require the hit to land on a box with the worst grade and say so in the prompt. Change the reveal highlight in DrillCard/Verdict to match, and add a unit test with a frame holding two boxes in different bins.

defects.issue: The occlusion and collaterals drills can be answered from which dataset subset a run comes from. In itemFor, positives are tagged runs, and these all come from the CoronaryDominance main set (dominance-main). Negatives must come from studies with no category, which means all of them come from the domain-shift subset (dominance). Measured: occlusion has 216 positives, all dominance-main, and 97 negatives, all dominance. Collaterals has 691 versus 329, split the same way. Because subset decides the label completely, a reader who picks up the look of the acquisition domain beats both drills. That conflicts with the stream goal of making the drills impossible to beat by guessing. The flaw was there before this stream, but S13 kept it.
defects.fix: Take negatives from the same subset as positives. For example, use the 43 main-set artefact studies that have no occlusion or collateral tag in any run, or stratify each set by subset as well as by label. If too few same-domain negatives exist, state the confound in the drill blurb and in the notes.

defects.issue: The constant-answerer acceptance test is tautological. Under summarise(), any constant answer gives balanced accuracy of exactly 1/|reference classes| and kappa 0, whatever the class mix, so the test would pass with no stratification at all. It never checks the per-class counts of makeSet sets or the constant answerer's raw accuracy. Two gaps follow. Plan sets are not stratified: always answering 'LAO cranial' scores 31.8% raw. In the view drill with 'accept', always answering 'AP' scores 25% raw against 1/9 chance, because scoreChoice rewrites ref to the chosen option for accepted neighbours. The report's claim that a constant answer 'scores chance in every drill' holds only for the balanced-accuracy metric as defined.
defects.fix: Add assertions that every makeSet set has equal counts per stratum, and that a constant answerer's raw accuracy is close to chance in the drills that are stratified. In the view drill, either report the constant-answer expected accuracy as 'chance' or note in the UI that borderline acceptance raises raw accuracy. Label the plan drill as unstratified (operator practice) in the set report.

defects.issue: On the Progress tab, the learning-curve reference line is drawn at 50% and labelled 'dashed line: 50%' for every drill. Chance is 25% in grade and estimate and about 11% in view and plan, so the curves suggest the wrong baseline.
defects.fix: Draw the reference line at each drill's chance level (1/K from the reference classes in that drill's results) and label it 'chance'.

defects.issue: Every drill answer writes an angio:<drill>:<runId> key into profile.quizMemory, including correct answers. The due counts in Dashboard and App.tsx therefore now include real-angiogram reads, but Review.tsx lists only quiz ids. Until integration step 4 is applied, the dashboard says 'N due' and the Review page shows nothing due. The notes document this.
defects.fix: Have the integrator apply integration step 4 (the Review.tsx button that calls requestDrill('review') and setSection('angio-real')). As an interim measure, consider writing only wrong reads to the SRS, or using a separate memory namespace.

defects.issue: Drill blocks carry params, and validate.ts checks them, but RealAngiograms only reads requested.drill, so the params are dropped silently. Content authors may expect a parameter such as a dataset or grade filter to take effect.
defects.fix: Either consume the params in Drills (for example, filter the candidate runs) or remove params from the schema and validator until they are supported.

missingScope: ARCADE segment-naming drill not built. The plan gates it on an approved download and licence confirmation, so leaving it out is acceptable; it is documented.

SimIds 'angio-real' and 'angio-pci' are not added to SimId or SIM_SECTION. useUiStore.ts was removed from this stream's owned list, so this is deferred with a workable diff; lessons link through the new drill block instead.

The plan's acceptance asked for the calibration drill on CoronaryDominance studies. It runs on CADICA instead, because CoronaryDominance has no stenosis labels; the deviation is justified and documented.
